To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CXCR6 is a novel negative regulator of hepatocarcinogenesis, which is dependent on natural killer T (NKT)- and CD4+T-cell-mediated senescence of tumor cells.
CXCR6 is an inhibitor of liver carcinogenesis, and that this effect is mediated by the ability of CXCR6 to recruit NKT and CD4+ cells to the liver and to promote the senescence of liver cells.
CXCR6 is expressed in a small subset of CD4(+) T-cells that have a memory phenotype and that CXCR6 deficiency results in a dramatic increase in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) incidence in mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the molecular mechanisms that regulate the development of liver cancer.
the development and evaluation of a new class of inhibitors of the CXCR4/CXCL12 axis.
the role of CXCR6 in the regulation of liver regeneration, hepatocarcinogenesis, and senescence.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CXCR6/CXCL16 axis is an attractive target to prevent or treat liver cancer.
CXCR6 has a significant role in the pathogenesis of HCC and is associated with the progression of HCC.
the CXCR6 receptor is expressed on the surface of T lymphocytes, and its expression is upregulated in response to the presence of CXCL16.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we identified CXCR6 as a novel suppressor of hepatocellular carcinoma.
CXCR6 promotes the accumulation of senescent cells, which are recognized and eliminated by NKT and CD4+T cells to prevent tumour formation.
CXCR6 is a negative regulator of hepatocarcinogenesis and that its expression in hepatocytes and hepatic stellate cells is required to control senescence in hepatocytes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CXCR6 is a negative regulator of liver cancer.
CXCR6 is a tumor suppressor in liver cancer.
CXCR6 is a key player in the control of senescence and that this control is dependent on NKT and CD4 T cells.
